races.title: State House, District 93
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Charlie Wallin
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for NC House District 93 (Ashe, Alleghany and Watauga counties). Born in Madison County, he has lived in Boone since 1990. He has worked at Appalachian State University for 26 years, most recently as Director of Retail Dining, and lists service as a Watauga County Commissioner.
cands.gaps: We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development or growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, gun laws, abortion, or policing. We could not find the dates he served as a Watauga County Commissioner or what he did in that role beyond his own statement that he advocated for a new 911 center and ambulance base. We found no independent news coverage of him, so his biography comes from his own campaign materials and a Ballotpedia survey he filled out. He has no known record of passing or sponsoring legislation.

local.label: Roots 100: He says he was born in Madison County and grew up there on a family farm, then moved to Boone in 1990 and has lived there more than 30 years.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Lists service as a Watauga County Commissioner and 8 years on the Watauga County Planning Board. He has been Director of Retail Dining at Appalachian State for about 26 years, a management role, and has not served in the state legislature.
qual.why: Local elected office and a long management career fit the middle band. He has no legislative service and no law, policy or budget career. Board and committee seats were not counted.
qual.label: Local elected office and a long management career fit the middle band. He has no legislative service and no law, policy or budget career. Board and committee seats were not counted.

cands.name: Ray Pickett
cands.bio: Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 93 since January 2021. Former owner and manager of the Blowing Rock Inn, with a career in hospitality management. Past president of the Rotary Club of Blowing Rock. He lives in Blowing Rock.
cands.gaps: We found no documented actions or statements by Pickett on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no list of the bills he sponsored. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any year. We could not confirm where he was born or raised, or the year he came to or settled in the High Country beyond "over 25 years". His campaign site says he served on the Blowing Rock Town Council and Planning Board, but no independent source we read confirms those terms or their dates. We found no endorsements beyond one minor voter-guide listing. No controversies turned up in the pages we read.

local.label: Roots 55: His campaign site calls him a native North Carolinian who has called the High Country home for over 25 years and lives in Blowing Rock; his upbringing is not documented.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since 2021, with appropriations work in his record. Before that he managed restaurants and other hospitality businesses and then owned and managed the Blowing Rock Inn.
qual.why: Several years of legislative service, including a seat on Appropriations, plus a business ownership and management career. He has no law or formal policy career, so the score sits at the lower end of the high band.
